Based on my analysis of the test image and 21 reference images:

**Test image observations:**
- Field-level view showing a stark contrast: healthy, lush soybean plants (left) vs. severely stunted, sparse plants with dramatically reduced canopy (right)
- Red flags mark both sections — typical of a susceptible vs. resistant variety trial or infested vs. non-infested plot
- The stunted plants on the right are alive but dramatically shortened with very few leaves and visible bare soil between plants
- No obvious leaf lesions, stem cankers, or mold — this is a systemic growth suppression pattern

**Comparison with references:**
- **SCN**: The top-left panel of its reference shows nearly identical sparse, thin rows of stunted plants in a field — best match
- **SDS**: Shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis on individual leaves plus root rot — not the same field-level stunting
- **Phytophthora/Charcoal Rot**: Plants die completely with brown coloration — test image plants are green but stunted
- **Pythium/Rhizoctonia**: Seedling-stage damping off — test plants are mature
- All leaf-spot diseases (Frogeye, Septoria, Bacterial Blight, etc.) don't match the field-level stunting pattern

The severe, patchy stunting affecting whole plants (not individual leaves/stems) at mature growth stage, visible as a row-by-row comparison, is the hallmark of **Soybean Cyst Nematode**.
